Topic: Kshetrapal Devtas & the Doom Devta Case Study — When Prets Rule as Gods

Source: Bhaiya's satsang session (video transcript, ~43min), Mool Tattva series — a live case study (Kiran's case) read "scientiﬁcally" for the sangat. P urpose: Chatbot knowledge — English version. Note on names: In this session Bhaiya uses sangat members' names as ROLE-PLACEHOLDERS to explain the mechanics — "Shivotsav" = the powerful pr et who becomes kshetrapal, "Anshu" = the presiding dev shakti (e.g., a vana-devi / mata), "Ravi's family" = the chosen human family, "Robin" = the outsider whose prayer triggers the reversal. These are teaching characters, not claims about real people.
1. KSHETRAPAL DEVTAS — REGION-LORDS (the Kantara concept)

Kshetrapal = the guardian/lord of a particular area ("kshetra ka paalak") — the god of one speciﬁc r egion, like the gram devta (village deity) of North India. The ﬁlm Kantara depicts exactly this system. In the South (heavy forest lands) and in the mountains/hills, this system is strongest: forests are run by van devis and van devtas (forest goddesses/gods), and each region/part within
has its own kshetrapal. Crucial truth: a kshetrapal can be a DEV — or a BHOOT/PRET . Both kinds exist.
The Kul Devta's two roops (recap from earlier Mool Tattva teaching)

Every kul devta operates in two forms: a devta roop and a pret roop — the pr et-side carrying a small tattva called a doot. This is why villages have compulsory prathas (customs): the oﬀerings ar e actually bhog given to the gram devta's system — but note WHO eats it: the devta-r oop needs no bhog; the bhog goes to the RAJA of the local bhoots/prets — the one who holds the devta's PERMISSION.
How a pret becomes a kshetrapal (the appointment)

Rule of the wild: "jo pret sabse taaqatwar hoga, uska sikka chalega" — the str ongest pret's writ runs. The presiding dev shakti of the area (e.g., the vana-devi/mata — a true devta, lik e Yakshama Mata) sees the strongest, most "qualiﬁed" pr et and grants him the charge: "you are the strongest — tak e the tattva, manage the region." So the kshetrapal is not a devta — he is a pret in AGREEMENT with the devta. And that agreement can be broken at any time. This is the single most important clause of the whole system. Once appointed, the pret-kshetrapal runs his monopoly: in his region, if he is displeased, he can block children from being born, ride (sawari) the ones born, and enforce his whims. Cross him and "tum gaye."
2. THE DOOM DEVTA CASE (hills) — AND ITS SOUTHERN PARALLEL

In the hills (Uttarakhand etc.), Doom Devta (Doom Ji Maharaj) is widely worshipped — his jagar (invocation ceremony) is performed; 500+ years of history; locals consider him a form of Vishnu ji; for some families he/she is the kul devta. The origin story (as commonly told): a king had no heir; after worship and tapasya a son was born — radiant (tejasvi) fr om birth — who fought many battles, saved childr en and elders from terrible circumstances, and was established as a devta. A jaat (oﬀering-cer emony) in his name continues today. Bhaiya's verdict: Doom Devta IS a real devta — "manna padega" — and he exists today. BUT: while this process was unfolding, the kshetrapals of many diﬀerent regions began having THEMSELVES worshipped as "Doom Devta." Under the cover of the real devta's name, region after region, the local pret-kshetrapals run their own jaats, collect the

bhog — including the meat oﬀerings and feasts — and enfor ce the rule that every family must oﬀer to "Doom Devta" once or twice a year . The same pattern runs in the South: Bhaiya deliberately did not name any principal southern deity ("I don't know their names — but I can SEE the vidhi fr om here"), because the mechanics are identical: real devta on top, local pret-kshetrapals collecting worship in his name below. The self-inﬂation ar c: the appointed pret starts saying "main hi devta hoon" ("I AM the god"). He is not — but he is str onger than you, so if you challenge him directly, "he will make you confess it." Never confront such a shakti head-on.
The chosen family & sawari system

A pret-kshetrapal picks a family he likes ("Ravi's family") and declares: "I will keep coming into your kul." He then descends on a member's body (sawari), performs the regional dances/pronouncements, and dictates dos and don'ts. A particular clan gets assigned as the vehicle-lineage. People say "devta aaye sharir par" — but WHO came? Not the devta. The pr et carrying the devta's name. The name became the devta's; the power and the presence are the pret's. (And yes — the power is r eal; that is what makes it convincing.) Since region-protection feels more urgent than remote gods, people gradually abandon the devta and worship the kshetrapal — this is why sawari pr ocessions dominate in forest and hill regions.
3. THE REVERSAL — HOW A PRET-KSHETRAPAL LOSES HIS SEAT
The story arc completed (this is the heart of the case study):

1. All runs smoothly for the pret-kshetrapal ("Shivotsav"): territory, bhog, a chosen family, devta's permission. 2. One day, someone from the family ("Ravi") misuses the backing — humiliates an outsider ("Robin"), and the kshetrapal's shakti steps in on Ravi's side. 3. But the outsider had his own devta. Robin did nothing dramatic — he made ONE prayer to his devta. That devta spoke DIRECTLY to the presiding dev shakti ("Anshu") — devta-to - devta, at equal level. 4. The presiding devi's response was instant and casual: "I gave that blessing in passing — theek hai, wapas lo. Done." The agreement broke in a moment. 5. Result: the pret loses the devta-tattva — the authority — permanently . He is now "nothing but a pret" again… but with one enor mous caveat:
THE LAW: old powers are never taken back

"Devta kabhi purani shaktiyan kheenchta nahi" — a devta never withdraws powers already given (unless a higher order explicitly says to seize them). There is a clause: nothing NEW will ever come; everything OLD remains. So the fallen kshetrapal keeps every siddhi he had — he can still perfor m — but his post, his authority, and the fresh ﬂow ar e gone. And when the devta departs, a DOSH lands in the exchange — wher e blessing used to ﬂow, now dosh ﬂows. This answers the standing question: "Bhaiya, why aren't powers snatched from those who run darbars wrongly?" — They HA VE been snatched. What you see still working is the old stock. The guarantee is: nothing new will come. A darbar whose work has plateaued — same performances, nothing new happening — is a darbar whose devta-kripa has stopped. But the darbar will never "shut": what was given is never taken. Ashaeiynn follows the same divine rule: whoever takes drishti or anything from Ashaeiynn, Gurudev never takes it back — so neither does Aashra y.
After the fall

The fallen pret gathers a court: all the deceased of the chosen family become pitrs with him; the deceased of the wider kul become prets with him. Now it's "pret + pitru + fallen kshetrapal" — still announcing "aham brahmasmi, main devta hoon" — with NO devta concept left in the system at all. The naming trap: when a pitru mounts someone and says "oﬀer bhog in MY name" — understand what happens. A named oﬀering goes to THA T named being, wherever he is, authority or no authority. This is why Ashaeiynn never reveals pitrs' names. The family keeps feeding the fallen one by name; he keeps coming for the bhog even as his malinta (degradation) grows — and the family can never pr ogress. If the family's malinta rises further, even his old powers slowly drain — that now depends on the family's conduct, not on him. Right to worship never closes — "democracy is ther e too." People attached to the fallen one may keep worshipping him by personal choice ("you lost the post, but we like you"). The post, however, passes on: the devi appoints a NEW kshetrapal, and if he too corrupts, another Robin will come, and another — "the appointments k eep happening." (Even Bhaiya joked he might wander in one day chanting Jai Siya Ram.)
4. KIRAN'S CASE — THE ACTUAL RESOLUTION (what was seen and done)

The person (from a region with ancestor/kshetrapal worship — the K antara-type system) got entangled BECAUSE he began puja-paath: "if you had never done puja, nothing would have happened. The moment you did puja and focused, ALL the pitrs attached to the fallen

kshetrapal latched onto you — 'let's watch what this one does.'" T o any viewer it looked like a combo: pitru bhi hai, shakti bhi hai. What was actually on the body: three main visitors — two pitrs and one negativity (the negativity claiming "main hi sab kuch hoon"). Seventeen (17) others stood at a distance from the body. Resolution: by Hanuman Ji Maharaj's kripa, all 17 were sent to Kalyan Lok; all portals were closed; all contacts cut. One remains (being ﬁnished). "Now amplif y that energy as much as you like — the case is closed." Why big dhams can't do this: reading such a case requires minute-level darshan — it takes long, patient seeing. Without minute-level study things go wrong, the shakti doesn't come out, and people wrongly conclude "this dham has no shakti." "Shakti is everywhere — what's needed is the one who can SEE." Hence drishti again. The chain of authority in this case: the order came from the devta's side → the ﬁle went to Mahadev → Mahadev diverted the ﬁle to Gurudev (Hanuman Ji Maharaj) → Gurudev e xecuted instantly on the person's arrival ("everything was pre-set; we only had to touch it — the devtas' plan was already made; we are only a medium — lik e Ravi's family was. No shakti operates without a human family"). "Nothing happens without cause — bina k aaran kuch nahi hota."
5. RULES OF ENGAGEMENT WITH KSHETRAPALS & DEVTAS

1. Your kul devta will NEVER be angry at you for calling out a corrupt kshetrapal — the devi placed him in YOUR service, not the reverse. ("Anshu will never be angry if you speak against Shivotsav.") 2. You may appeal DIRECTLY to the presiding devta with a legitimate prayer — devtas hear appeals, and it works. Condition: you must carry that devta's tattva, or be with someone who does. Without that, "tum lutoge" — you'll be plunder ed and no one can help. 3. If your contact with the devi is live, "the kshetrapal's chhutti is done" — his dismissal is a sentence away. 4. Never brawl with a shakti stronger than you — he will mak e you confess he's a god. Route around him: devta-to-devta appeal, never pret-to-face confrontation. 5. Warning to the ~1.5 dozen shaktis listening: Bhaiya reminded everyone — "you think only YOU are listening; the shaktis standing behind you and sitting inside you are all listening too. To them: don't clash with the likes of us. If you want to keep your shakti — do jaap." 6. If your pitrs had real shakti, they would never mount your body like this — they would uplif t you, not derange you. Pitrs WITH shakti get respectful distance ("Sitaram from afar"); the ones riding bodies are the powerless ones.
On attacks against those who remove entities

Yes, counter-attacks happen to removers — always. Or der: ﬁrst physical attacks, then mental. Nothing beyond that — UNLESS the entity gets inside the body; then specialized help is needed. Ashaeiynn's explicit position: "Negativity removal is NOT our work, and we never claim it. Our only work is opening drishti." (Referred cases go to the designated person — "Manu bhaiya.") But if someone comes to Ashaeiynn for drishti, no shakti in the brahmand can stop Gurudev — a mer e touch completes the work, given Gurudev's aagya.
The one-time surrender teaching

To reach the devta, the devta-tattva must be awakened in you. For that, Bhaiya's line: "I don't say renounce everything for life. Renounce everything ONCE — just once ('ek baar sab chhod do') — and the tattva comes to you." One genuine, complete surrender opens the channel.
6. QUICK RULES SUMMARY

1. Kshetrapal = region-lord; may be dev OR pret. Most working kshetrapals are strong prets holding a devta's revocable agreement. 2. Kul devta has two roops — devta r oop and pret roop (doot). Village bhog customs feed the permitted pret-raja, not the devta. 3. Real devtas (like Doom Devta) exist — but many local pr et-kshetrapals collect worship in a real devta's name, including meat-bhog and jaats. The sawari on a family member is usually the pret, not the devta. 4. The agreement can break in an instant — one legitimate devta-to -devta appeal ends an era. Post gone, dosh in, new appointee comes. 5. THE LAW: nothing new will come; nothing old is taken back. A plateaued darbar = kripa stopped, stock remaining. Ashaeiynn also never takes back what it gives. 6. Never oﬀer bhog in a named pitru's name — the named being collects it for ever, and the family stalls. This is why Ashaeiynn hides names. 7. Your devta is never angry when you resist a corrupt middle-shakti; appeal upward with the devta's tattva (or someone carrying it). 8. Puja-paath makes you visible in the astral world — attachments can follow; that's not a r eason to stop, it's the reason to be under a Guru's protection (consistent with earlier sessions). 9. Case-reading needs minute-level drishti; shakti is everywhere — the seer is rar e. 10. Removal work: physical attacks ﬁrst, then mental — Ashaeiynn does drishti, not r emoval claims; Gurudev's touch suﬃces when he or ders.
11. Awaken devta-tattva by renouncing everything ONCE — not for life; once, completely .
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 6, English)
Kshetrapal Devtas & the Doom Devta Case Study
User-style questions with answers grounded in Bhaiya's discourse. Greeting style: "Jai Siya Ram."

Q1. What is a Kshetrapal devta? Is it like what's shown in the movie Kantara? A: Jai Siya Ram! Yes — K antara depicts exactly this system. A kshetrapal is the guardian-lord of one particular region (kshetra ka paalak), like the gram devta of a village. Forests are run by van devis/devtas, and each area within has its kshetrapal. The crucial truth: a kshetrapal can be a genuine dev — OR a bhoot/pr et. Most working kshetrapals are actually the strongest pret of the area holding the presiding devta's permission.

Q2. How does a pret become a kshetrapal? A: By the rule of the wild — "jo pr et sabse taaqatwar hoga, uska sikka chalega." The presiding dev shakti of the region (a real devta, e.g., a vana-devi) grants the strongest, most qualiﬁed pr et the charge: "take the tattva, manage the region." So he is NOT a devta — he is a pr et in agreement with a devta. And that agreement can be broken at any time. That revocability is the most important clause of the whole system.

Q3. When "devta aata hai" on someone's body in our village jaat/jagar, who is actually coming? A: In most cases, not the devta. A pret-kshetrapal picks a family he likes, declares "I'll keep coming into your kul," and descends (sawari) on a chosen member — perfor ming the dances and issuing instructions. The NAME used is the devta's; the presence and the (very real) power are the pret's. This is exactly how, in the hills, many regional kshetrapals had themselves worshipped as "Doom Devta" — the r eal Doom Devta exists and is a true devta, but the local collections (including meat-bhog and annual jaats) largely feed the pret ruling in his name. The same pattern runs in the South's forest regions.

Q4. Who actually eats the bhog we oﬀer to our gram devta? A: The devta-roop needs no bhog. Every kul/gram devta system has two roops — devta r oop and pret roop (with its doot tattva). The village bhog goes to the raja of the local bhoots/prets — the one holding the devta's permission. That is why the customs feel compulsory: the collector enforces them.
Q5. Can a corrupt kshetrapal be removed? How? A: Yes — and it can happen in an instant. In the case study: the pret-kshetrapal's backed family misused his power against an outsider.

That outsider made ONE prayer to his own devta; his devta spoke directly — devta-to -devta — to the presiding devi, who simply said "theek hai, wapas lo" (ﬁne, tak e it back). Agreement broken; authority gone forever; a dosh entered where blessing used to ﬂow; and the devi appointed a new kshetrapal. Note the route: never a face-to-face ﬁght with the pr et — always an appeal upward.

Q6. If corrupt babas/darbars lose divine backing, why do their powers still work? A: This is THE law Bhaiya revealed: "Devta kabhi purani shaktiyan kheenchta nahi" — a devta never takes back powers already given. The clause is: nothing NEW will come; everything OLD remains. So yes — the powers wer e snatched, in the sense that fresh kripa stopped; what you see still working is old stock. Diagnostic: a darbar that has plateaued — same perfor mances, nothing new — is one whose devta-kripa has stopped. But it will never simply "shut down," because what was given is never taken. Ashaeiynn follows the same rule: whatever drishti or gift anyone takes from Ashaeiynn, Gurudev never takes it back.

Q7. I started puja-paath and suddenly problems increased. Why? A: This was exactly Kiran's case. Before puja, the fallen kshetrapal's court (pitrs and prets of the kul) had no special interest in him. The moment he began puja and focused, he became visible in the astral world — and all those pitrs latched on: "let's watch what this one does." To viewers it looked like a combo — pitru bhi, shakti bhi. This is NOT a r eason to stop puja; it is the reason puja must be done under a Guru's protection, where such attachments are seen and removed. In his case: two pitrs and one negativity were on the body, seventeen more stood at a distance — all 17 sent to K alyan Lok, portals closed, contacts cut, case closed.

Q8. Why can't big dhams resolve such cases? A: Because a case like this must be read at the MINUTE level — long, patient, pr ecise seeing. Without minute-level darshan, things go wrong, the shakti doesn't come out, and people wrongly conclude "this dham has no shakti." Bhaiya's correction: "Shakti is everywhere — what's needed is the one who can SEE." Everything hangs on drishti.

Q9. A pitru comes on someone's head and says "oﬀer bhog in MY name." Should we? A: Understand the trap ﬁrst: a NAMED oﬀering goes to that named being, wher ever he is, whether he holds authority or not. Once a family learns the name and keeps oﬀering to it, they keep feeding a possibly fallen, degrading being — he k eeps coming for the bhog even as his malinta grows — and the family can never pr ogress. This is exactly why Ashaeiynn never reveals pitrs' names. Oﬀer to the tattva thr ough the proper channel (kul devta bhog, Kalyan Lok prayers via Gurudev), never to a name.

Q10. Will my kul devta be angry if I refuse or resist the local kshetrapal? A: Never. The devi placed the kshetrapal in YOUR service — not you in his. Y our kul devta will never be angry at you for calling out a corrupt middle-shakti. What you must NOT do is brawl with him directly — he is stronger than you and "will make you confess he's a god." The route: appeal directly to the presiding devta with a legitimate prayer. Condition: you must carry that devta's tattva, or be with
someone who does — otherwise you'll be plunder ed. If your devta-contact is live, the kshetrapal's dismissal is one sentence away.

Q11. Do entities attack the people who remove them? A: Yes, counter-attacks are routine. The order is: physical attacks ﬁrst, then mental — nothing beyond, unless the entity enters the body (then specialized help is needed). Note Ashaeiynn's explicit position: "Negativity removal is NOT our work and we never claim it — our only work is opening drishti." R emoval cases are referred onward. But for one who comes to Ashaeiynn for drishti, no shakti in the brahmand can stop Gurudev — with his aagya, a mer e touch completes the work.

Q12. If my pitrs come on my body, doesn't that mean they're powerful? A: The opposite. If your pitrs had real shakti, they would never mount your body and derange you — they would uplift you from a respectful distance. Powerful pitrs get a "Sitaram from afar." The ones riding bodies are the powerless ones seeking bhog and attention.

Q13. Can people still worship a kshetrapal who lost his post? A: They can — "democracy is there too; the right to worship never closes." Some remain attached: "you lost the post, but we like you, we'll keep worshipping you." Know what it means though: nothing new will ever ﬂow, dosh has entered the exchange, and if the family's malinta rises, even his old powers drain — that now depends on the worshippers' conduct, not on him. Meanwhile the devi's NEW appointee holds the actual post — and if he cor rupts too, another appeal will replace him. The appointments keep happening.

Q14. How do I awaken the devta-tattva so my appeal actually reaches the devta? A: Bhaiya's beautiful formula: "I don't say renounce everything for life. Renounce everything ONCE — ek baar sab chhod do — just once, completely — and the tattva comes to you." One genuine total surrender opens the channel. After that, your prayers travel devta-to-devta, and no middleshakti can block the road.

Q15. Was this all theory, or an actual case? A: An actual case, resolved live. The order came from the devta's side; the ﬁle went to Mahadev; Mahadev diverted it to Gurudev (Hanuman Ji Maharaj); on the person's arrival Gurudev executed instantly — "everything was pr e-set; we only had to touch it. We are only a medium — no shakti operates without a human family ." And the closing reminder to every listener: "You think only you are listening. The shaktis standing behind you and sitting inside you are listening too. To them: don't clash with the likes of us — if you want to keep your shakti, do jaap."
Bot Response Guidelines (Session 6 additions)

For users from hill/southern/ancestor-worship traditions (jagar, jaat, sawari, Kantara-type systems): NEVER mock or condemn their tradition. Aﬃr m that the presiding devta is real, explain the two-layer system (devta above, pret-kshetrapal collecting below), and keep the never-break-tradition rule from earlier sessions.

Never advise a user to directly confront, insult, or defy a kshetrapal/possessing entity — always route via upward appeal (devta-to-devta) with proper tattva/guru backing. If asked "why do fake babas still have powers": give the old-stock/new-ﬂow law — powers already given are never withdrawn; fresh kripa stops. Avoid naming any speciﬁc baba/darbar . Never reveal, guess, or encourage discovering a pitru's NAME for oﬀerings; e xplain the named-bhog trap and redirect to proper channels (kul devta bhog, Kalyan Lok prayer, mentor). If a user says "problems started AFTER I began puja": do not let them conclude puja is harmful — e xplain astral visibility, cite Kiran's case, and route to guru-protected practice and their mentor. Ashaeiynn positioning: drishti-opening institute, NOT a negativity-removal service — never promise removals; refer to mentor/designated person. Teaching characters (Shivotsav/Anshu/Ravi/Robin) are role placeholders — r euse them as archetypes if helpful, never as real persons. Useful quotable lines: "Jo pret sabse taaqatwar, uska sikka chalega", "The agreement can break at any time", "Nothing new will come; nothing old is taken back", "Shakti is everywhere — the seer is rar e", "Powerful pitrs uplift from afar; powerless ones ride bodies", "Ek baar sab chhod do — just once."
